Reading the map

Paper roof — healthy, quiet
Amber roof — work outstanding
Blue roof — being built
Red roof — blocked
Red base — a blocker inside
Slate base — your decision inside
Amber base — items queued
Amber line, slow flow — degraded link
Red line, never flows — broken link
Dot at the wall — the link joins here
Arc over a line — a crossing, not a join
Fly closer: labels gain their counts
Drag to orbit · scroll to zoom · click a box
Flow animates the planned links with moving dots (explanatory, not live data). Trace walks the declared critical path one step at a time. Stack lifts the three levels apart.
The left rail groups parts by lane (planning order), not by map position. Counts on boxes and rows are open items: work recorded against a part and not yet closed.

This is your codebase, as a city

so you always know what it does, how it’s architected, and what needs work next

Buildings are modules — color is status: paper is healthy, amber owes work, blue is being built, red is broken. Pipes are connections that know what flows through them.

Moving around

Orbitdrag · trackpad: one-finger click + drag Pantrackpad: two-finger click + drag · mouse: right-drag · touch: two fingers Zoomscroll or pinch (nothing shrinks with distance — it magnifies) HomeR or Reset — glides back to the flat view

Interrogating

A buildingclick to energize it — add more and only the live circuit flows; click again to cut A pipeclick to read what data flows across it Groundclick to restore the whole board TopbarFlow animates the data · Trace tells the story · Stack lifts the levels
